title: Generative data-engine foundation model for universal few-shot 2D vascular image segmentation (UniVG)
mechanism: Decomposes thin structures and backgrounds and recombines them with varied morphology, then adapts the generator with a few labelled images to synthesise realistic image-label pairs.
adaptation: Recombine crack skeletons from ARTS/CFVS with CSIR half-cut canvases (GDI twins or crack-free pool cells), adapt the renderer on 478 cells; reuse the recipe, not the vascular checkpoint. Repo stated as forthcoming (github.com/XinAloha/UniVG), not verified.
min_experiment: PF + recombined crack/background pairs vs PF. Metric E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: < +0.02.
evidence: R: 11 vessel tasks across 5 modalities with 5 labelled images each; comparable to fully supervised; UniVG-58K pretraining set.
prior_overlap: CP100 pasted real crack pixels (n.d.); structure/background recombination with a learned renderer is untested. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: ARTS/CFVS crack skeletons onto CSIR half-cut canvases (inpainted twins), adapt the renderer on 478 cells.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Recombined set vs PF. Metric E1 relF1@2. Kill: < +0.02. About 15 GPU-h.
